# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 74 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic Equivalence)

**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** P.Mich. 130, Shepherd of Hermas 74 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_074_page_001.jpg

---

## Similitude 9, Part 1 — The Vision of the Twelve Mountains

**74:1** After I had finished writing down the commandments and similitudes of the shepherd — the angel of repentance — he came to me again and said: "I want to show you everything the Holy Spirit spoke with you in the form of the church. That Spirit is the Son of God."

**74:2** "You were weak in the flesh, and the truth hadn't been fully explained to you yet. Speak with the Power and it will all become clear — because that Power is strong and divine, belonging to glorious and mighty virtue."

**74:3** I said to him: "Lord, please — show me everything you promised to show me." He led me to Arcadia, to a certain hill, and had me sit down on it. He stood facing me.

**74:4** I saw a vast plain, and ringing the plain were twelve mountains, each one different in form. The first mountain was covered with black rocks. The second was bare — no vegetation at all. The third was choked with thorns and brambles. The fourth had vegetation that was half dead — the tops of the plants were green but the roots were dry, and some plants had been burned away by the sun. The fifth was grassy but rugged terrain. The sixth was riddled with cracks, some small and some large, with grass growing in the crevices.

**74:5** The seventh mountain was lush and bright — the whole thing was in full bloom. Cattle and birds of every kind grazed and fed there, and the more they ate, the more the vegetation grew and multiplied. The eighth mountain was full of springs, and every creature of the Lord drank from those springs.

**74:6** The ninth mountain had no water at all — completely barren — and it was crawling with wild beasts and deadly reptiles that preyed on human beings. The tenth mountain was covered with great trees, completely shaded, with sheep resting and chewing their cud in the shade.

**74:7** The eleventh mountain was thickly forested, and every tree was loaded with various kinds of fruit — whoever saw them would want to eat. The twelfth mountain was pure white, radiant and joyful to look at, beautiful in every way.

---

*PNEUMA renders for contemporary clarity and accessibility, making the elaborate twelve-mountain vision that opens Similitude 9 vivid and comprehensible.*
